lessons.title: Agronomy Fundamentals
lessons.summary: A multipart introduction to soil science and farm management for Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. Explore soil formation, chemistry, nutrient retention, and the soil food web, with practical field exercises.

downloads.label: Lesson 1 — Soil Science & Farm Management (PDF)
downloads.summary: How soil forms and varies across a farm, including soil horizons, texture, structure, water, roots, soil biology, and pH. Includes a two-location field observation and a frozen-ground alternative.

downloads.label: Lesson 2 — Soil Chemistry & Cation Exchange (PDF)
downloads.summary: Understand cation exchange capacity, nutrient retention, acidity, and lime. Includes a worked pasture soil-test example and a practical plan for sampling separate management zones.

downloads.label: Lesson 3 — The Soil Food Web (PDF)
downloads.summary: Explore bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, and other soil organisms, and follow nutrients from decomposing residues into plants. Connect soil habitat, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium cycling with pasture management and the food we harvest.

lessons.audience: Livestock owners, pasture managers, and beginning agronomy students.
overview: Understand the soil beneath your farm and how it supports plant growth, animals, and everyday management decisions. This class brings core soil science together with practical observations for Michigan’s Upper Peninsula.

Begin with Lesson 1 on soil science, continue to Lesson 2 on soil chemistry and cation exchange, then explore the soil food web in Lesson 3. Each PDF is free to read, download, and print. More lessons will be added as the class grows.
learning_objectives: Understand the factors that form soil.
Compare sand, silt, and clay, and distinguish soil texture from structure.
Explain how soil pore space affects water, oxygen, and roots.
Understand the basics of soil pH and nutrient availability.
Compare contrasting farm sites and use observations and soil tests to guide management.
Explain how soil organisms cycle nutrients and how soil habitat affects their availability to plants.

lessons.title: Pasture and Grazing Fundamentals
lessons.summary: Ten lessons connecting pasture plants, livestock needs, and grazing decisions in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. Learn to assess paddocks, budget forage, plan rotations, and adapt through the seasons.

downloads.label: Lesson 1 — How Pasture Plants Grow (PDF)
downloads.summary: Grass anatomy, photosynthesis, and seasonal growth. Connect leaves, roots, and soil conditions with the way pasture plants develop.

downloads.label: Lesson 2 — What Grows in a Pasture (PDF)
downloads.summary: Identify the roles of grasses, clovers, and other broadleaf plants, and understand how grazing and growing conditions change a forage mixture.

downloads.label: Lesson 3 — What Happens After a Bite (PDF)
downloads.summary: Explore how leaf removal, stored carbohydrates, and repeat grazing affect plant recovery, and why equal rest periods can produce different results.

downloads.label: Lesson 4 — How to Tell When a Paddock Is Ready (PDF)
downloads.summary: Assess plant development, ground firmness, and the residual left after grazing. Recognize wet-ground damage and judge readiness across a paddock.

downloads.label: Lesson 5 — How Much Forage Is Available? (PDF)
downloads.summary: Estimate forage on a dry-matter basis, distinguish standing mass from usable feed, and build a budget that accounts for residual and grazing losses.

downloads.label: Lesson 6 — How Much Forage Does the Herd Need? (PDF)
downloads.summary: Estimate herd dry-matter demand and combine it with available forage to calculate herd-days and allocation size using worked examples.

downloads.label: Lesson 7 — Designing Paddocks and a Grazing Rotation (PDF)
downloads.summary: Distinguish stocking rate from stock density, plan fences and water access, and calculate rotation intervals while allowing for changing recovery needs.

downloads.label: Lesson 8 — Grazing Through an Upper Peninsula Year (PDF)
downloads.summary: Follow spring thaw, summer slowdown, fall stockpiling, and winter feeding, with attention to soil conditions, forage access, and nutrient distribution.

downloads.label: Lesson 9 — Why Pastures Thin Out (PDF)
downloads.summary: Use plant patterns, field history, and soil tests to investigate thinning pasture, then match changes in grazing, traffic, or reseeding to the cause.

downloads.label: Lesson 10 — A Year in the Life of a Grazing Farm (PDF)
downloads.summary: Bring the class together in a fictional farm’s seasonal forage budget, including changing strip sizes, fall stockpile, and winter hay inventory.

lessons.audience: Beginning graziers, livestock owners, and homesteaders planning or improving pasture.
overview: Follow pasture from the growth of a grass plant to the feed budget for a whole grazing year. These ten lessons connect soil conditions, forage supply, animal demand, and everyday management decisions in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula.
Read the lessons in order, or return to individual topics as needed. Each two-page PDF is free to read, download, and print. The course builds on soil concepts introduced in Agronomy Fundamentals.
Cedar Run Farm is a fictional teaching example. Its herd, acreage, forage values, and calculations illustrate the methods; they are not measurements or recommendations for Tripple B Farms.
learning_objectives: Explain how pasture plants grow and recover after grazing.
Recognize how forage species and ground conditions affect paddock readiness.
Estimate usable forage and herd demand on a dry-matter basis.
Plan paddock allocations, water access, and recovery intervals.
Adapt grazing and stored-feed plans through an Upper Peninsula year.
Investigate pasture thinning and match management changes to the cause.

lessons.title: Livestock Nutrition Fundamentals
lessons.summary: Eight lessons on cattle nutrition, connecting forage digestion, feed quality, and animal needs. Learn to interpret hay tests, compare feeds, and work through a seasonal feeding plan.

downloads.label: Lesson 1 — How Cattle Digest Forage (PDF)
downloads.summary: Understand the four stomach compartments, rumination, and the microbes that turn forage into usable nutrients. Connect forage structure and feed changes with rumen function.

downloads.label: Lesson 2 — Dry Matter and Feed Intake (PDF)
downloads.summary: Compare pasture, hay, and supplements on a dry-matter basis, distinguishing feed offered, feed consumed, and inventory used. Includes worked intake and feeding-loss calculations.

downloads.label: Lesson 3 — Energy, Protein, and Fiber (PDF)
downloads.summary: Interpret energy, crude protein, and fiber measures on a cattle feed report, and explore how forage quality and intake together affect nutrient supply.

downloads.label: Lesson 4 — Reading a Hay Test (PDF)
downloads.summary: Define and sample a hay lot, interpret as-fed and dry-matter report values, and compare hay purchases by dry matter and estimated energy supplied.

downloads.label: Lesson 5 — Water, Minerals, and Vitamins (PDF)
downloads.summary: Explore dependable water access, mineral delivery, vitamin sources, and species differences. Includes a worked example of tracking mineral disappearance.

downloads.label: Lesson 6 — Feeding Cattle at Different Life Stages (PDF)
downloads.summary: Relate maintenance, growth, pregnancy, and lactation to feeding needs. Use body condition and feeding records to investigate changes and plan feeding groups.

downloads.label: Lesson 7 — Supplementation and Ration Arithmetic (PDF)
downloads.summary: Identify a nutrient shortfall, calculate a possible supplement contribution, account for displaced forage, and compare costs within the whole diet.

downloads.label: Lesson 8 — A Winter Feeding Plan for Cedar Run (PDF)
downloads.summary: Bring hay inventory, nutrient supply, cold-weather conditions, feeding access, and spring turnout together in a fictional farm’s winter feeding case.

lessons.audience: Beginning cattle owners, livestock keepers, and homesteaders learning the foundations of forage-based feeding.
overview: Build an understanding of how cattle use forage and how feed quantity, quality, and access affect nutrition. These eight lessons progress from rumen digestion and dry matter to feed reports, life stages, supplementation, and winter planning.

Each lesson is a separate two-page PDF, free to read, download, and print. The class connects with Agronomy Fundamentals and Pasture and Grazing Fundamentals, following the link from soil to forage to animal nutrition.

Cedar Run Farm, its feed values, and its ration calculations are fictional teaching examples. The lessons focus on cattle; requirements and mineral suitability differ between livestock species. Worked examples illustrate methods rather than prescribe a ration for a real herd.
learning_objectives: Explain how cattle digest forage and why feed structure matters.
Convert feed amounts between as-fed and dry-matter bases.
Interpret energy, protein, fiber, and hay-test measurements.
Understand water access and the role of minerals and vitamins in a feeding program.
Relate feeding needs to life stage, body condition, and actual intake.
Work through supplement comparisons and a winter hay inventory example.
